teaser: Cloudflare runs agents and controls them; its own writing leaves room for a signed record of what each agent was asked to do.
core_idea: Cloudflare is both where agents are built and run (Agents SDK, sandboxes, AI Gateway, remote MCP) and where they are controlled (Access for MCP portals, WriteGuard risk tiers, DLP, Web Bot Auth). It has controls at every layer, mostly with open defaults and some in beta. Its own Agent Access Model and trusted-delegation post argue that a scope says what an agent may do, not what it was asked to do or who answers for it. An Agent Behaviour Policy is that per-agent, signed record, and Cloudflare's logs are what it can be checked against.
